newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trygg-Hansa/Forenade Liv form sales co.
newsitem.headline: Trygg-Hansa/Forenade Liv form sales co.

text.p: Swedish insurer Trygg-Hansa and Forenade Liv on Tuesday announced an agreement to form a jointly owned company for sales and administration of group insurance plans.
"The company will start out with a premium volume of nearly 500 million crowns," the two companies said in a statement.
"This will be made possible through the transfer of Trygg-Hansa Mutual Life Insurance Company's and Forenade Liv's portfolios of voluntary group life and group sickness insurance to the new company."
They said the two companies have agreements with groups and organisations in Sweden to which around two million people are affiliated.
The new company would offer products related to life, non-life, savings, health and welfare segments, they said.
Trygg-Hansa spokesman Mats Hoglund said in the statement that the new company created potential for volume growth.

"Forenade Liv cooperate very effectively with various types of organisations and companies. This, combined with Trygg-Hansa's offering of comprehensive insurance and banking products, forms a strong base for futher developments," he said.
Forenade Liv president Kjell-Ake Persson said the new company will enable his group to broad its group insurance coverage.

"Since we will now have the opportunity to apply group insurance techniques toward entirely new insurance solutions, we will be able to offer our customers more comprehensive insurance cover at a lower cost," he said.
The deal is conditional on approval from regulatory bodies, they said.
Forenade Liv insures around 1.2 million people through its group insurance policies, which is its main business area, a Trygg-Hansa spokeswoman told Reuters.
The Stockholm-based mutual life company, which is owned by its customers, employs a staff of about 135, she said.
